why: Aaron McCarlson's apartment is a small second-floor flat in a Northside apartment block just north of the Longshore North fast travel point, with an outside intercom beside its front door. The building shell, the flat's furniture and devices and the street around it are base-world geometry, but the street story's quest section - Aaron's standing spot, the community spawner, the corridor/scene triggers and the quest collision area - only streams from the unrun gig, so in the clean slate the flat is empty. This proposal restores that section and puts Sergeant Aaron McCarlson at home in his relaxed default stand-around pose, and leaves out the gig's recording scene, Johnny Silverhand's post-fight spots, the combat phase and the q003 noise the catalogue attached through a shared TV ref.

open_questions: Walk up to Aaron McCarlson's flat north of the Longshore North fast travel point and check the door opens. Vanilla seals and force-closes #nid_07_door_aaron, and the outside intercom is gig-scripted, so the runtime door policy is the only way in.
Look inside the flat and check Aaron is there. He should stand at his own spot in a relaxed stand-around pose, calm and alone, not missing, hostile, duplicated or left out on the street.
Check the flat reads as a normal residence, not a quest scene. There should be no Johnny Silverhand, no recording confrontation setup, no combat state, no body and no post-fight loot staging.

Check nothing in the flat starts the unrun gig. The TV carries the q003 #tv_1_q003 tag and the intercom is the gig's call button, so no prompt should offer to play the recording, call Aaron or begin "Scrolls before Swine".
Walk the flat's corridor and room and check the collision_area toggle left no invisible wall. If V or Aaron is blocked or falls through the floor, flip collision_area to 1 and re-check.

If the flat renders as a bare shell, check whether the parent openworld prefab is also required. This proposal loads only the nested street-story section; a missing interior would mean the parent #loc_sts_wat_nid_07b_aaron_mccarlson_apartment_openworld must be added as a second prefab.

communities.why: The flat's only occupant: Sergeant Aaron McCarlson at his own spot inside the apartment, standing around in the relaxed generic stand-around workspot. Vanilla activates exactly this entry phase in the always-running open-world story phase, so it is the normal at-home state; the post-gig default_after (sitting at a diner table far south) and the recording_scene (angry stand) are quest outcomes and are not used.

variant_toggles.why: The street-story's quest collision area is off in normal play: vanilla's open-world story phase (and the district phase that owns the same toggle) hides it, and only a quest scene raises it. Setting it to 0 reproduces vanilla's pre/post-gig state and keeps no invisible barrier around the flat or its corridor.

proximity_wait.why: The flat's only entrance, a DoorControllerPS with a resolved full path in the building's own gameplay/devices section, on the normal way into the apartment. It is a device, not a workspot, and it streams with the building so the second community activation lands once the flat and Aaron's spot have streamed in.
